title: Implicit Network Boundary (The Waldo Fallacy)
pattern: An interface or trait definition containing methods that return generic, non-network-aware error types (such as `Result<T, ()>` or basic local enums) implemented by a struct that performs synchronous network RPC/HTTP calls.
why_bad: It violates the Waldo principle of distribution by treating remote calls identically to local memory lookups [28, 291]. Remote calls have radically different failure modes (timeouts, packet loss, socket resets) and latency characteristics (milliseconds vs. nanoseconds) [102, 113]. Hiding these behind a generic local interface prevents upstream callers from reasoning about network partitions, setting deadlines, or handling retries safely [90, 113].
detection: Identify Trait definitions that do not return a network-aware error type (e.g., enums representing connection reset, timeout, or DNS failure) or do not accept timeout/context parameters, which are implemented by structs invoking networking libraries (e.g., `reqwest`, `hyper`, `tokio::net`).
fix: Modify the trait signature to explicitly accept a timeout/deadline (or async context) and return an error type that represents network-specific failure conditions, forcing callers to implement appropriate fault tolerance [90, 113].
source: Martin Kleppmann, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications*, Chapter 4 (RPC) / passages [112, 113]; Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!*, page 210-214 / passage [291]; Alex Petrov, *Database Internals*, Chapter 8 / passage [28].
